title: How long is the line after each halving?
description: A line sixteen units long is halved once, twice and three times, and each length is written as a power of two. The video shows that dividing by two takes one two away from the power, and Keeko doubts what halving three times divides by.
teaching_notes: One idea: dividing a power of two by a smaller power of two cancels twos, so the exponent goes down by that many. Watch for students who add the halvings to get a divisor, or who divide the exponents.

source: A line is 16 units long. Find its length after halving it once, twice and three times, as powers of 2.
video_script.why: A learner sees why dividing powers of the same base takes the exponents away, by cancelling twos.
video_script.substitution: the book's own line of sixteen units, halved once, twice and three times
video_script.anchor: a line of sixteen units drawn on the board and erased half at a time
video_script.wrong_move: adds the three halvings as two and two and two to get the divisor six
video_script.payoff_line: Each halving takes one two away from the power of two

final_answer.value: 8 units (2³), 4 units (2²) and 2 units (2 to the power 1)
final_answer.spoken: eight units, four units and two units

maths_rules: halving 3 times divides by 2 x 2 x 2 = 8, and 16 / 8 = 2
slip: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 adds the halvings instead of multiplying the twos
video_script.design: One idea: dividing cancels twos. Wrong idea: three halvings divide by six. The line is erased half at a time and the twos cancel in pairs; the last length only appears at the answer.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a line 16 units long on the board

marks.line: a line marked 16 units long is drawn
marks.half: half of the line is erased, and then half of what is left
marks.ask: three marks stand ready for the lengths after the halvings

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='line'/>A line is sixteen units long.
<bookmark mark='half'/>We erase half of it. Then we erase half of what is left, and half again.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How long is the line after one, two and three halvings?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 16 = 2 x 2 x 2 x 2 = 2^4, with the 2 labelled base and the 4 labelled exponent

marks.names: the 2 is labelled base and the 4 is labelled exponent

narration: <bookmark mark='twos'/>Sixteen is two times two times two times two.
<bookmark mark='power'/>We write that as two to the power four.
<bookmark mark='names'/>The two is called the base, and the four is called the exponent.

beats.on_screen: Given: a line of 16 units = 2^4 units, halved once, twice, three times

marks.given: the line of 16 units is written as 2^4 units

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a line of sixteen units, which is two to the power four, halved three times.

beats.on_screen: To find: the length after each halving, as a power of 2

marks.find: the words length after each halving, as a power of 2 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the length of the line after each halving, as a power of two.

marks.divide: 2^4 / 2 is written with the four 2s above and one 2 below
marks.cancel: one 2 above is cancelled with the 2 below

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step one, halve the line once, which divides two to the power four by two.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>The two below cancels one of the four twos above.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Three twos are left, which is two cubed. The line is eight units long.

marks.cancel: two 2s above are cancelled with the two 2s below

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step two, halve the line twice, which divides two to the power four by two squared.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>The two twos below cancel two of the four twos above.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Two twos are left, which is two squared. The line is four units long.

beats.on_screen: three times: 2^4 / 2^3 = (2 x 2 x 2 x 2) / (2 x 2 x 2); the exponents 4 take away 3

marks.cancel: three 2s above are cancelled with the three 2s below
marks.rule: 2^(4 - 3) is written, the result is left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='divide'/>Step three, halve the line three times, which divides two to the power four by two cubed.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>The three twos below cancel three of the four twos above.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The exponents show it too. Four take away three is the exponent that is left.

marks.ans: the three lengths 8 units, 4 units and 2 units are written in a row

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Each halving takes one two away from the power of two.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The line is eight units, then four units, then two units long. The last one is two to the power one.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6, divide by 6, struck out; 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 beside it

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble shows 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 and a division by 6

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks halving three times is dividing by six, because two and two and two make six.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But each halving divides by two, one after another. Three halvings divide by two times two times two, which is eight.
<bookmark mark='all'/>Sixteen divided by eight is two. The halvings multiply the divisors, they do not add them.
